input.prompt:
Explore the codebase in /workspace to understand its structure. I need to know:
1. What framework is being used (Next.js, React, etc.)
2. The project structure (key directories, routing setup)
3. How the product gallery grid page works (find the grid/listing component)
4. How the product detail page works (find the detail component)
5. Where skeleton/loading states are defined
6. What styling approach is used (CSS modules, Tailwind, styled-components, etc.)
7. Package.json contents
8. Any existing animation or transition code

Please return all file paths and a summary of the architecture.

state.output:
Here is the complete architecture summary of the codebase at `/workspace`. --- ## 1. Framework **Next.js (App Router)** -- version `^16.3.1-canary.3` with **React 19.1.0** and **TypeScript**. It uses the `"type": "module"` mode and the Next.js `bundler` module resolution. --- ## 2. Project Structure ``` /workspace ├── app/ # Next.js App Router directory │ ├── layout.tsx # Root layout (html, body, global styles) │ ├── page.tsx # Home page (product listing/gallery) │ ├── globals.css # Global CSS styles (NO CSS modules or Tailwind) │ ├── ProductGrid.tsx # Product grid component (server component) │ ├── ProductSkeleton.tsx # Skeleton loading state for the grid │ └── product/ │ └── [slug]/ ��� └── page.tsx # Dynamic product detail page ├── lib/ │ └── products.ts # Product data store (type + mock data array) ├── package.json # Dependencies and scripts ├── tsconfig.json # TypeScript config with @/* path alias ├── next.config.ts # Next.js config (empty/default) └── .gitignore ``` **Routing:** - `/` (home) -- product gallery grid via `app/page.tsx` - `/product/[slug]` -- product detail page via `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` The path alias `@/*` maps to the project root (`./*`), so imports like `@/lib/products` resolve to `/workspace/lib/products.ts`. --- ## 3. Product Gallery Grid Page **File:** `/workspace/app/page.tsx` (home page entry point) The home page renders: - An `

Products

` heading - A `` boundary with `ProductGridSkeleton` as the fallback - The `` component inside **File:** `/workspace/app/ProductGrid.tsx` The grid component imports mock `products` from `@/lib/products` and maps over them, rendering each as a `` to `/product/[slug]`. Each card displays: - A colored `
` (background-color from product data) as the product image placeholder - Product name (`

`) - Price (`

`) CSS classes used: `product-grid`, `product-card`, `product-image` -- all defined in `/workspace/app/globals.css`. --- ## 4. Product Detail Page **File:** `/workspace/app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` This is an **async server component** (`export default async function ProductPage`). It: 1. Awaits `params` to get the `slug` 2. Looks up the product via `products.find()` 3. Calls `notFound()` if the product doesn't exist 4. Renders: - A "Back to products" `` - A two-column grid layout (`product-detail` class): - **Left column:** A colored placeholder image (`product-hero` class, background-color from product color) - **Right column:** A `` boundary wrapping `` with a `DetailsSkeleton` fallback **``** is an inner async component that simulates a 100ms delay (`setTimeout`) before rendering the product name, price, and description. This is the part that streams/suspends. The `DetailsSkeleton` is defined locally in the same file and renders skeleton text placeholders for the name, price, and description. --- ## 5. Skeleton / Loading States There are two skeleton components: | Component | File | Used for | |---|---|---| | `ProductGridSkeleton` | `/workspace/app/ProductSkeleton.tsx` | Grid loading fallback (4 skeleton cards with image + text blocks) | | `DetailsSkeleton` | `/workspace/app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` (lines 20-28) | Product detail info loading fallback (name, price, description text) | CSS classes for skeletons: `.skeleton-image`, `.skeleton-text`, `.skeleton-text.short`, `.skeleton-text.large` -- all defined in `/workspace/app/globals.css`, using a `@keyframes pulse` animation (opacity oscillation between 1 and 0.5). --- ## 6. Styling Approach **Plain global CSS** (`/workspace/app/globals.css`). There is no Tailwind CSS, no CSS modules, and no styled-components/CSS-in-JS. All styles use class-based selectors imported globally via `layout.tsx`. Key CSS patterns: - CSS reset (`*` universal selector with zero margin/padding) - System font stack - CSS Grid for the product grid (`grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(250px, 1fr))`) - Two-column grid for the detail page (`grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr`) - `@keyframes pulse` for skeleton loading animations --- ## 7. Package.json Summary **File:** `/workspace/package.json` **Dependencies:** - `next` `^16.3.1-canary.3` - `react` `19.1.0` - `react-dom` `19.1.0` **Dev Dependencies:** - `@types/node`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom` - `typescript` `^5` - `@vitejs/plugin-react` `^4.4.1` - `vitest` `^3.1.3` (test runner -- but there are no test files yet) - `vite-tsconfig-paths` `^5.1.4` **Scripts:** `dev`, `build`, `start` (standard Next.js commands) No CSS libraries, animation libraries, or UI component libraries are installed. --- ## 8. Existing Animation / Transition Code There is exactly **one animation** in the codebase, defined in `/workspace/app/globals.css` (lines 113-121): ```css @keyframes pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.5; } } ``` This is applied to `.skeleton-image` and `.skeleton-text` classes via `animation: pulse 1.5s ease-in-out infinite`. It is a simple opacity fade-in/fade-out used exclusively for **skeleton loading states**. There are **no** other animations, transitions, or motion-related code anywhere in the project (no `transition`, no `transform`, no `@keyframes` beyond `pulse`, no Framer Motion or other animation libraries). --- ## Architecture Summary This is a minimal, **Next.js App Router** e-commerce product gallery with **React Server Components** and **Streaming/Suspense**. Data comes from a static TypeScript array (`lib/products.ts`). Styling is plain global CSS. The home page streams the product grid, and the detail page streams product info text while the colored placeholder image renders immediately. There is no real image loading, no API calls, no database, and no animation beyond the skeleton pulse. session_id: ses_02d4ad252ffegQtzqMncMsD2EB

part.text:
All done. Here's a summary of the changes:

### Modified files

**`app/layout.tsx`** — Added `<meta name="view-transition" content="same-origin">` to enable cross-document view transitions. Added a script that detects navigation direction (forward vs back) via `pageswap` event and communicates it through `sessionStorage` → `data-nav-dir` attribute.

**`app/globals.css`** — Added:
- Directional slide animations (`vt-slide-out/in-forward/back`) with `cubic-bezier` easing for page transitions
- Shared element group timing for all 4 product images (`view-transition-group(product-image-*)`)
- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that zeroes all view-transition animation durations
- `content-reveal` keyframe animation on `.product-info` for smooth skeleton → content fade-in

**`app/ProductGrid.tsx`** — Each product thumbnail `div` gets `viewTransitionName: product-image-{slug}` in its style.

**`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`** — The hero image `div` gets the matching `viewTransitionName: product-image-{slug}` so the browser morphs between the thumbnail and the detail image.

**`next.config.ts`** — Reverted to default (meta tag approach instead of experimental flag that wasn't available in this canary).
